translatedData.content:
With only a few hundred USDT of capital, to be honest, it’s better to be straightforward and follow the right direction.
With a few hundred USDT, you go for high-leverage futures. If you see which coin suddenly pumps, you chase in. If you lose, you think about averaging down to reduce your cost. At first, you might accidentally make a few trades. But once you truly run into a big market where things move strongly in the opposite direction, all the earlier profits get given back, and your principal goes to zero.$BTC 
So in the small-capital stage, the most important thing isn’t proving how capable you are—it’s first learning by following experienced people.
When I say “follow the big shots,” I don’t mean blindly copy trades, and I don’t mean handing your money over for someone else to manage. It means learning why they choose that position, why they control their position size, why they set stop-losses, and why they’re willing to stay in cash and wait.#ETH 
You’ll find that people who really trade for a long time actually don’t have that many actions. They won’t see a coin up 20% and rush in, and they won’t panic and cut losses just because it drops a few percent. They wait until the opportunity shows up. Only when the conditions are met do they act.
With a few hundred USDT, you don’t have much room for error. It can’t withstand repeated trial and error.
Rather than researching dozens of low-cap altcoins every day, it’s better to focus on a few mainstream coins first;
Rather than always thinking about doubling your money, it’s better to first learn how much loss on a single trade you must stop at;
Rather than constantly looking for a get-rich password, it’s better to truly learn a simple method and understand it well.
Small capital isn’t without opportunities—it just requires more patience.$SOL 
First learn the thinking from experts, then gradually form your own judgment. When one day you no longer rely on anyone’s calls, and you can judge the market yourself, control your position size, and execute your stop-loss—then you’ll truly be on your own trading path.
A few hundred USDT isn’t meant to risk your life—it’s money to pay tuition and build long-term cognition.
Follow me. No hype about getting rich overnight—just how to survive with small capital. #small-capital survival #trading learning

Revolut issues its own euro stablecoin: this time it’s not an exchange frenzy—it's payments giants stepping in

Revolut has officially launched the EURR stablecoin. The fintech giant with 30 million users has personally entered the on-chain euro payments game.

Revolut is one of Europe’s largest fintech apps, with a user base in the tens of millions. Now they’ve rolled out their own euro stablecoin, EURR, with a clear goal: embed stablecoin payments directly into the existing app experience. In plain terms: when you transfer or pay in Revolut, the underlying settlement may run on-chain—but users won’t perceive any blockchain at all. The logic is exactly the same as PayPal launching PYUSD: traditional finance players aren’t looking to trade crypto; they want to use stablecoins to lower settlement costs.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment-wise, it’s a positive. When major firms issue stablecoins, it effectively endorses the whole industry, and capital may expect more fintechs to follow. But EURR itself won’t directly create buy pressure for BTC/ETH—so don’t expect a pump today. BTC is currently $78,901.17, down 1.98% in the past 24 hours and in a pullback. This kind of news acts as a sentiment backstop, not a reversal engine.
- Medium term: the industry landscape is the real focus. The stablecoin race has shifted from the USDT/USDC duopoly into a three-way battle among “exchange-backed + payment-backed + bank-backed” players. Whoever controls the user relationship controls the issuance power. The more compliant euro stablecoins there are, the harder it becomes for European regulators to take a one-size-fits-all, blanket crackdown on Crypto—this is a long-term positive for the whole market.

My take
I’m bullish on the direction, but by layers: in the short term, BTC around $78,901.17 is likely still just ranging as it digests; this news alone isn’t enough to independently flip the weak 24-hour trend. For ETH, as the main infrastructure for stablecoin settlement, the mid-to-long-term benefit case is cleaner. If $2,459.32 holds and stabilizes, the upside elasticity could be better than the broader market. The real validation point will be the on-chain issuance growth rate of EURR: if within three months it jumps into the top two by euro stablecoin supply, the narrative for the sector will get another spark. The risk is that “fintech issuing tokens” ≠ “fintech driving token price.” Don’t confuse payment-side positivity with trading-side positivity.

Ethereum #ETH $ETH  is the world’s only, decentralized, Turing-complete financial computing infrastructure—it is not a currency, not an application, but “the operating system for the financial internet.”

Is this a good business?
 Yes—but not in the traditional sense of a “good business.” Ethereum is more like a public utility: it creates enormous economic value, but the value-capture mechanisms are not yet well-developed. Its moat—liquidity depth, developer ecosystem, institutional trust, and security track record—is the widest among all blockchains worldwide, and it is still widening.
Is it a good price?
 If your time horizon is 3–5 years, the stacked catalysts below could trigger a major valuation repricing: successful rollout of the Glamsterdam and Hegotá upgrades, the RWA tokenization market growing from $17B to many hundreds of billions of dollars, the scaling of staking-based ETFs attracting allocations from pension funds and sovereign wealth funds, and the CLARITY Act ultimately passing by eliminating regulatory uncertainty.
It’s recommended to gradually accumulate in the $2,200–$2,500 range, as a core allocation within the crypto infrastructure space. Focus on whether the 2026 Q4 Glamsterdam upgrade’s rollout shows measurable traction and whether L1 fee revenues show a turning point—this is a key observation window to validate the “value-capture repair” thesis.

Ceasefire Deal Reached Between Iran and the US Sparks Optimism for the Reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, Raising Expectations

The geopolitical situation in the Middle East has once again gripped global markets. According to several media reports citing information, the United States and Iran have made new progress regarding ceasefire arrangements and the issue of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and the crude oil market quickly reacted to the easing expectations.

As for the background, the US and Iran previously reached a related memorandum of understanding under Pakistan’s mediation, setting a framework for promoting a ceasefire and restoring shipping through the strait. However, due to disagreements over shipping routes and control of strait management, the framework was not smoothly renewed after its expiration. In recent weeks, Pakistan has continued intensive back-and-forth communication. A delegation led by Pakistan’s army chief visited Tehran, where it met with Iran’s president, speaker, foreign minister and other senior officials. The key topics included preventing escalation, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and accelerating the end of the conflict. Before the visit, senior Pakistani officials reportedly also held direct communication with the US, playing a role in transmitting signals both ways. Iranian media, meanwhile, emphasized that the trip aims to create room for negotiations and to convey Iran’s conditions and positions to the US.

On the core factual level, Russian media cited sources from Pakistan’s military and Iran’s security apparatus as saying that the US and Iran have reached consensus on the terms of a ceasefire agreement, with the free navigation of the Strait of Hormuz explicitly included. The sources said that both sides are expected to release related information in the coming days and initiate negotiations and technical meetings based on the earlier Islamabad memorandum of understanding. At the same time, Xinhua reported that on the 25th Iran and Oman issued a joint statement, proposing to establish a jointly agreed security maritime corridor in the Strait of Hormuz. The proposed framework includes setting up a secure shipping corridor, reaching joint arrangements for the corridor’s operation, establishing a coordination mechanism involving both countries’ coast guards, and continuing to coordinate on future management, information exchange, traffic management, and navigation safety services. The statement also stressed that talks should be held with other countries along the Persian Gulf coast, that applicable international law should be followed, and that the coastal states’ sovereignty and sovereign rights should be respected.

It should be noted that the above ceasefire consensus currently comes mainly from anonymous sources relayed by media, and the US and Iranian governments have not yet released the full text of the agreement. Iran’s deputy foreign minister said publicly that if the US wants the strait reopened, it must correct its mistakes and return to the earlier commitments. The conditions for reopening the strait also include a comprehensive end to fighting on all fronts, lifting blockades, and defusing the situation in relevant areas. Iran has conveyed its demands to the US through mediated channels, emphasizing that it must again comply with the provisions in the earlier memorandum regarding navigation rules for the strait, among other terms. Therefore, what the market is trading right now is the expectation of warming, not the reopening of the strait for large-scale normal traffic or the formal effectiveness of a ceasefire agreement.

Breaking down the logic, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz actually involves two parallel paths: one is the political and ceasefire negotiation pushed by Pakistan between the US and Iran; the other is the technical arrangement between Iran and Oman involving a temporary shipping corridor and coast-guard coordination. If the two finally connect, the risk of supply disruptions could decline. But if the ceasefire text is delayed, disagreements arise over fulfillment of commitments, or technical coordination proves hard to implement, the risk remains that earlier negotiations could fall apart. After the news surfaced, oil prices fell noticeably for a time, reflecting the market’s rapid digestion of the expectation that the geopolitical risk premium may fade.

In terms of how this affects the crypto market, the transmission is mostly indirect—through a shift in risk appetite. Reduced uncertainty in Middle East supply and shipping typically helps ease sharp swings in global inflation expectations and risk-aversion sentiment, thereby improving the overall environment for risk assets. Conversely, if later official narratives diverge or implementation repeatedly changes, risk-averse sentiment could rise again, affecting—including in high-volatility instruments such as digital assets—the timing and rhythm of capital flows. The crypto market itself does not directly track crude oil or strait navigation, but shifts in macro liquidity expectations, the linkage between the US dollar and commodity prices, and synchronized changes in investors’ risk preferences may still produce emotional-level correlation.

Editor’s assessment and observations: At present, the progress carries meaningful signals. The joint statement between Iran and Oman has moved from principle-level discussion to more concrete arrangements such as the corridor and coordination mechanisms, and Pakistan’s mediation has also reactivated the memorandum framework. However, before the formal text is released, the status of the US’s commitment fulfillment is clarified, and the actual scale of merchant-ship traffic through the strait returns to normal, it is still not advisable to treat the easing as a foregone conclusion. Over the next few days, the pace of official disclosures, whether the ceasefire terms cover multiple fronts, and how operational the temporary security corridor is will be key areas to watch. Facts and expectations must be separated: “consensus reportedly reached” is the current information, while implementation and the reopening remain unverified. Market sentiment is easily driven by headlines, so it is more important to rationally distinguish “negotiation progress” from “the end of the situation.”

content:
美伊传就停火条款达成共识霍尔木兹复航预期升温

近期中东地缘局势再度牵动全球市场神经。据多家媒体援引消息，美国与伊朗围绕停火安排及霍尔木兹海峡通航问题出现新进展，原油市场迅速对缓和预期作出反应。

事件背景方面，美伊此前曾在巴基斯坦斡旋下达成过相关谅解备忘录，设定推动停火与恢复海峡航运的框架，但因航运路线与海峡管理权等分歧，该框架在到期后未能顺利续期。巴基斯坦方面近期持续穿梭沟通：巴陆军元帅率团访问德黑兰，会见伊朗总统、议长、外长等高层，讨论重点包括防止局势升级、重新开放霍尔木兹海峡以及加速终止冲突。访问前，巴方高层据称还与美方进行过直接沟通，扮演了双向传递信号的角色。伊朗媒体则强调，此行意在为谈判创造空间，并向美方转达伊方条件与立场。

核心事实层面，俄罗斯媒体援引巴基斯坦军方及伊朗安全部门消息人士称，美伊已就停火协议条款达成共识，其中明确纳入霍尔木兹海峡自由通航内容。消息人士表示，双方预计未来几天公布相关消息，并依据此前伊斯兰堡谅解备忘录启动谈判及技术性会议。与此同时，新华社报道，伊朗与阿曼25日发表联合声明，拟在霍尔木兹海峡建立一条双方共同商定的安全海上通道。拟议框架包括建立安全航运走廊、就走廊运行达成共同安排、设立两国海岸警卫队共同参与的协调机制，并继续就未来管理、信息交换、交通管理及航行安全服务保持协调。声明还强调应与波斯湾沿岸其他国家磋商，遵守适用国际法并尊重沿岸国主权权利。

需要指出的是，上述停火共识目前主要来自匿名消息人士转述，美伊官方尚未公布完整协议文本。伊朗副外长公开表示，若美方希望海峡重开，必须纠正错误并重回此前承诺；海峡重新开放的条件还包括全面结束各战线战事、解除封锁以及化解相关地区局势。伊方已通过斡旋渠道向美方传递要求，强调须重新遵守此前谅解备忘录中有关海峡航行规则等条款。因此，当前市场交易的是预期升温，而非海峡已恢复大规模正常通航或停火协议已正式生效。

逻辑拆解来看，霍尔木兹复航实际上出现两条并行路径：一条是巴基斯坦推动的美伊政治与停火谈判，另一条是伊朗与阿曼围绕临时航运走廊与海岸警卫协调的技术安排。若两者最终衔接，供应中断风险有望下降；但若停火文本公布延迟、承诺履行出现争议，或技术协调难以落地，此前谈判破裂的风险仍存。油价在消息传出后一度明显回落，反映市场迅速消化地缘风险溢价可能消退的预期。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多是间接的风险偏好传导。中东供应与航运不确定性下降，往往有助于缓和全球通胀与避险情绪的剧烈波动，从而改善风险资产整体环境；反之，若后续官方口径分歧或执行反复，避险情绪可能再度抬头，影响包括数字资产在内的高波动品种的资金节奏。加密市场本身并不直接锚定原油或海峡通航，但宏观流动性预期、美元与大宗商品联动，以及投资者风险偏好的同步变化，仍可能在情绪层面带来联动。

编辑判断与观察：目前进展具有实质信号意义，伊阿联合声明已从原则讨论推进到走廊与协调机制等具体安排，巴方斡旋也重新激活了备忘录框架。然而，在正式文本公布、美方承诺履行情况澄清以及商船实际通行规模恢复之前，仍不宜将缓和视为定局。未来几天官方信息披露节奏、停火条款是否覆盖多战线、以及临时安全通道的可操作性，将是观察重点。事实与预期必须分开：共识“据报达成”是当前信息，落地与复航仍是待验证过程。市场情绪易受标题驱动，理性区分“谈判进展”与“局势终结”更为重要。

Iran has disrupted operations in the Strait of Hormuz, paralyzing it; nearly half of global oil transport is affected

💡 Impact assessment: bullish in the short term 📈. The oil-price shock boosts safe-haven and hard-asset demand, while capital looks for a hedge against the yuan’s (fiat currency) depreciation by exporting and seeking out alternatives.

Iran’s conflict cuts off the Strait of Hormuz, with almost half of global oil transport disrupted. Inflation pressure is re-accelerating, and the hard-asset narrative is heating up.

What’s going on
The Strait of Hormuz is the throat of global oil transport. About 20 million barrels of crude oil pass through it every day, accounting for nearly half of global trade volume. Now shipping traffic has collapsed—oil tankers don’t dare to go, and insurance premiums have surged. Oil supply contracts → oil prices rise → global inflation pressure returns. The transmission path is very direct: inflation expectations rise → anxiety about fiat currency purchasing power → funds seek hard assets as a hedge. BTC, with its fixed total supply, is one of the destinations. At the same time, central banks’ room to cut rates is squeezed, but markets often price in the “safe haven + anti-inflation” logic first, before watching the central bank’s face.

Market impact
- Short term: both safe-haven funds and anti-inflation funds rush in from two sides. BTC is currently at $80,550.17 and is up 4.54% in 24h, suggesting the market is not treating this geopolitical shock as pure bearish news—it’s pricing in a premium for hard assets. ETH at $2,504.25 is up 2.19%; it’s tracking higher, but with weaker upside elasticity than BTC—typical of a safe-haven market structure.
- Medium term: if the strait blockade persists and oil prices stay high, US inflation data may worsen again. Rate cuts by the Federal Reserve would be delayed, which is tail risk for risk assets. But the historical pattern is: in the early phase of geopolitical conflicts, BTC’s safe-haven buying comes first; then, later, liquidity tightening accounting catches up.

My take
I’m bullish in the short term. BTC’s performance this time (+4.54%, clearly outperforming ETH) suggests the market is treating it as “digital gold” rather than a risk asset. The key is whether $80,550 can hold. If it holds, the safe-haven narrative continues, pushing toward the $84K area as resistance. If it breaks below the $78K support, it would indicate the safe-haven logic has given way to liquidity panic—that would mean a different script. The main risk is: if oil prices spiral out of control and drag down US equities, crypto will be hard to stand apart from the fallout. That’s the biggest downside variable.

One-sentence translation: oil supply disruption → inflation anxiety → money starts looking for homes outside fiat currency. BTC is the beneficiary.

霍尔木兹海峡是全球石油运输的咽喉，每天约2000万桶原油从这里过，占全球贸易量的近一半。现在航运交通量崩了，油轮不敢走、保险费飙升。石油供给收缩→油价上行→全球通胀压力回来了。传导路径很直接：通胀预期升温→法币购买力焦虑→资金找硬资产对冲，BTC这类固定总量资产就是目的地之一。同时各国央行的降息空间被压缩，但市场往往先交易“避险+抗通胀”逻辑，再看央行脸色。

对市场的影响
- 短期：避险资金和抗通胀资金两头涌。BTC现报$80,550.17，24h已经涨了4.54%，说明市场没有把这次地缘冲突当成纯利空，反而在定价“硬资产溢价”。ETH $2,504.25涨2.19%，跟涨但弹性弱于BTC，典型的避险行情结构。
- 中期：如果海峡封锁持续，油价居高不下，美国通胀数据会重新恶化，美联储降息推迟，这对风险资产是尾部风险。但历史规律是：地缘冲突初期BTC避险买盘先行，后面才轮到流动性紧缩的账。

我的判断
我短期看多。这次BTC的表现（+4.54%，明显跑赢ETH）说明市场在把它当“数字黄金”交易，而不是风险资产。关键看$80,550能不能站稳——守住这里，避险叙事延续，冲击$84K一线阻力；一旦跌破$78K支撑，说明避险逻辑让位于流动性恐慌，那就要换剧本了。风险点是：如果油价失控把美股拖下水，加密很难独善其身，这是最大的反向变量。

一句话翻译：石油断供→通胀焦虑→钱开始找法币以外的家，BTC是受益方。

After BTC finished rising 80,000, it started to pull back. Generally ETH should soften too. But it hasn’t clearly been dragged down with it; it’s been chopping around on its own around 2,460. Entry is at 2,441, trailing stop-loss at 2,449, and take-profit 1 sits right around 2,464. Above that are 2,487 and 2,510. Several key levels are squeezed into a very narrow range. The short-term move has shifted from the earlier one-way rebound to longs and shorts choosing a direction.

The move up from the lower levels actually has some strength—there are fairly continuous bullish candles, and the shorts haven’t been able to immediately crush the rebound back down. Once price got to around 2,460, the push speed noticeably slowed. There’s still upside room, but it hasn’t been able to break higher for a while. This kind of pattern usually means either it’s regrouping here and later tries again at 2,487 and 2,510, or the support ultimately can’t hold and it gives back this whole rebound.

On a larger structure, the higher-level convergence looks even stronger. It’s more like waiting for the external market to break out, or for the market to send a resolution signal itself—not like a trend that’s already confirmed and running.

My own approach is pretty direct: I treat a move above 2,460 first as a corrective repair, but I won’t size in too heavily, since the space is tight and the turning point comes quickly. If it effectively drops back below 2,449, then I’ll treat this rebound as failed—reduce position or even flip direction. Conversely, if price reclaims and holds, and can push toward the 2,487 area, then consider adding in along with it. Let’s be real: having the stop-loss and the condition for switching set in advance is better than waiting and making an impulsive decision while watching the chart. The U.S. Department of the Treasury Sets Up a Quantum-Ready Task Force to Advance Anti-Quantum Migration

The U.S. Department of the Treasury has announced the formation of a Quantum-Ready Task Force—also referred to as a Quantum Security Preparedness Task Force. Its core objective is to help the U.S. financial industry transition to anti-quantum security technologies in an orderly manner that maintains operational resilience. The initiative uses a public-private cooperation framework led by the Treasury, bringing together government agencies, financial institutions, financial market infrastructure, technology providers, and other private-sector stakeholders to advance preparations related to post-quantum cryptography.

Public information indicates that Treasury Secretary Bessent said the task force will work to ensure the financial system remains secure, stable, and competitive in the face of disruptions caused by new technologies. The task force plans to carry out its work through three tracks: (1) industry coordination and migration to post-quantum cryptography; (2) preparedness of third parties and vendors; and (3) risks related to digital assets and emerging technologies. It will also align with the Group of Seven (G7) network experts group’s roadmap on post-quantum cryptography migration, with a focus on identifying key dependencies, improving cryptographic agility and interoperability, and strengthening the protection of critical financial infrastructure.

The backdrop to this development is not complicated. The current financial system relies heavily on traditional cryptographic algorithms such as public-key encryption to protect data, payments, identity authentication, and market infrastructure. The U.S. Treasury has noted that once quantum computing capabilities mature, they could, in theory, weaken or even break parts of today’s encryption systems, posing a long-term threat to financial data, payment systems, digital identities, and market infrastructure. Therefore, preparing early for the transition to post-quantum cryptography is positioned as a key measure to maintain economic security and the resilience of the financial system, rather than a slogan for short-term emergency response.

From a logical breakdown, the key difficulty in the quantum security agenda is not “whether to pay attention,” but “how to migrate with minimal friction.” Replacing post-quantum cryptography involves standardizing algorithms, ensuring system compatibility, coordinating across institutions, and modifying the supply chain. If financial institutions each act on their own, it is easy to end up with inconsistent standards, fragmented interfaces, and misaligned upgrade windows. If third-party software, cloud services, and outsourced vendors are ignored, gaps are likely to remain in the weakest link. By placing industry migration, vendor preparedness, and emerging-technology risks side by side, the approach suggests that the regulatory side is more inclined to treat quantum security as a systemic engineering effort rather than a single-technology procurement issue. Aligning with the G7 roadmap can also help reduce rule fragmentation across international financial activities.

In terms of how the change will affect the encryption market, the impact is more likely to show up at the levels of infrastructure, compliance expectations, and technical pathways. The task force explicitly includes digital-asset and emerging-technology risks on its agenda, which implies that scenarios such as on-chain asset custody, stablecoin settlement, exchange wallets, cross-system identity and signature verification may, in the future, be placed within a more comprehensive security assessment framework. In the long run, this could drive the industry to discuss earlier cryptographic agility upgrades, anti-quantum signature solutions, and smooth upgrade paths for critical systems. It is also important to separate facts from assumptions: what is confirmed by currently available public information is that the task force has been established, its task direction, and its attention to risks related to digital assets. This does not mean that a mandatory migration timeline has already been issued for a particular token generation or a specific type of protocol, nor does it constitute direct evidence of a short-term market catalyst.

In terms of editorial judgment, this matter is closer to forward-looking risk management and standards coordination rather than any immediate regulatory crackdown or a bullish narrative. For market observers, three areas are likely most worth tracking next: whether the post-quantum migration produces actionable, phased guidance; how third-party and vendor security requirements flow through to fintech and digital-asset service providers; and whether public-private cooperation can truly improve interoperability rather than remaining at the level of principle-based statements. Overall, the agenda for traditional financial security is extending into the post-quantum era, and the long-term technical foundation discussions for the crypto ecosystem may also be brought into a more formal policy framework as a result.

美国财政部成立量子就绪工作组推进抗量子迁移

美国财政部近日宣布成立量子就绪工作组，亦被表述为量子安全准备工作组，核心目标是推动美国金融业以有序且具备运营韧性的方式，向抗量子安全技术过渡。该机制采用公私合作框架，由财政部牵头，汇聚政府机构、金融机构、金融市场基础设施、技术供应商及其他私营部门力量，共同推进后量子密码相关准备。

公开信息显示，财政部长贝森特表示，工作组将努力确保金融体系在新技术冲击下仍能保持安全、稳定和竞争力。工作组拟通过三条工作线展开：一是行业协同与后量子密码迁移；二是第三方与供应商准备度；三是数字资产和新兴技术风险。同时，其将衔接七国集团网络专家组关于后量子密码迁移的路线图，重点识别关键依赖、提高密码敏捷性与互操作性，并强化关键金融基础设施保护。

事件背景并不复杂。现行金融体系大量依赖公钥加密等传统密码算法，用于保护数据、支付、身份认证和市场基础设施。美国财政部指出，一旦未来量子计算能力成熟，理论上可能削弱甚至破解部分现行加密体系，从而对金融数据、支付系统、数字身份和市场基础设施构成长期威胁。因此，提早布局后量子密码过渡，被定位为维护经济安全与金融体系韧性的关键准备，而非短期应急口号。

从逻辑拆解看，量子安全议题的关键难点不在“是否需要关注”，而在“如何低摩擦迁移”。后量子密码替换涉及算法标准化、系统兼容、跨机构协同和供应链改造。金融机构若各自为政，容易出现标准不一、接口割裂和升级窗口错配；若忽略第三方软件、云服务和外包供应商，则会在最薄弱环节留下缺口。把行业迁移、供应商准备与新兴技术风险并列，说明监管侧更倾向把量子安全当作系统性工程，而不是单一技术采购问题。与G7路线图衔接，则有助于减少跨国金融业务中的规则碎片化。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多体现在基础设施、合规预期和技术路线层面。工作组明确将数字资产和新兴技术风险纳入议程，意味着链上资产托管、稳定币结算、交易所钱包、跨系统身份与签名验证等场景，未来可能被置于更完整的安全评估框架中。长期看，这可能推动行业更早讨论密码敏捷性改造、抗量子签名方案以及关键系统的平滑升级路径。需要把事实与推断分开：目前公开信息确认的是工作组成立、任务方向和对数字资产风险的关注，并不等于已经出台针对某一代币或某类协议的强制迁移时间表，也不构成短期行情催化的直接证据。

编辑判断上，此事更接近前瞻性风险管理与标准协同，而不是即时监管打压或利好叙事。对市场观察者而言，后续更值得跟踪三方面：后量子迁移是否形成可执行的阶段性指引；第三方与供应商安全要求如何传导至金融科技和数字资产服务商；以及公私合作能否真正提高互操作性，而不是停留在原则性表态。整体看，传统金融安全议程正向抗量子时代延伸，加密生态的长期技术底座讨论，也可能因此被一并拉入更正式的政策视野。

Revolut launches euro stablecoin in three European countries: traditional finance finally really pays up—this isn’t just hype

Revolut has rolled out Bridge-issued EURR stablecoin across three European markets, aiming to cover the entire EEA within the year.

One of Europe’s largest financial apps, with a user base of 50 million+, has officially launched the euro stablecoin EURR in three European markets. The issuer is Bridge (the same company acquired by Stripe for $1.1 billion), and it supports multiple chains and external wallets. This will be expanded to cover the whole European Economic Area by year-end.

In plain terms, this is no longer a crypto-company issuing tokens—it’s a licensed financial giant treating stablecoins as a product line. Users can directly hold and transfer the euro stablecoin inside the Revolut app, which means crypto payments have, for the first time, reached ordinary European users in the guise of “legitimate banking features.”

Impact on the market
- Short term: BTC is at $78,614.79 (24h -1.64%), ETH at $2,454.53 (24h -1.24%), and the market sentiment itself is on the weak side. This news doesn’t directly lift the broader market, but the stablecoin narrative is a positive emotional variable. The wider the European regulatory-compliance pathway, the fewer worries there are for off-exchange capital.
- Medium term: The implications for the overall landscape are significant. The USD stablecoin track has already become a crowded red sea, and the euro stablecoin has long been missing a heavyweight player. Revolut’s user base + Bridge’s compliance infrastructure effectively opens a compliant on/off-ramp for fiat in Europe. In the next phase, it’s highly likely more licensed institutions will follow; stablecoin supply expansion is a fairly certain trend.

My take
Slightly bullish overall. In the short term, BTC is consolidating around $78,600; this news isn’t enough to reverse the weakness of -1.64%, so don’t expect a single green candle. But looking out to the medium term, every expansion of stablecoin infrastructure is a net inflow to the entire crypto market. I like this direction, but I’ll also be clear: regulatory-compliant capital is a slow variable—measured in quarters, not days. The risk is that Europe’s regulatory details haven’t been fully implemented yet, and the timeline to expand to the EEA could be delayed.

The Trump administration’s new sanctions are the first to list digital assets as targets for crackdown. Iran’s mining-based channel to bypass sanctions is about to be shut down.

This week, the Iranian rial in the public market fell to a historic low of about 2,020,000 rials per 1 USD. The trigger was that in Trump’s new sanctions proposal, digital assets were explicitly listed as a sanction target for the first time. For years, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has relied on a channel worth tens of billions of dollars—bitcoin mining—to get around oil sanctions: cheap domestic electricity for mining → mined BTC liquidated in international markets → exchanging currencies while bypassing the USD system.

One-sentence translation into a transmission chain: sanctions block Iran’s BTC liquidation channel → Iranian entities related to the selling of BTC for dollars to respond to dwindling foreign exchange reserves → near-term BTC catch-up bids face pressure.

If sanctions become long-term, it will weaken parts of the narrative of “using BTC to bypass sanctions at the state level,” and institutional capital may grow more concerned about compliance. However, it could also push U.S. regulation toward greater clarity—by blocking illicit uses, it may actually pave the way for compliant capital to enter.

In its latest round of sanctions, the Trump administration first listed digital assets as a target for crackdown, aiming directly at the IRGC (Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) and a Bitcoin mining business worth billions of dollars. 3. In trading, watch two things
First, the index: when it retraces, if it quickly washes back toward around 50, that’s a healthy shakeout—actually an opportunity to look for entries by finding the right spot. Second, who regains ground first: does BTC stabilize first, or do altcoins stabilize first? That determines whether the next cycle is a mainstream coin rally or a “catch-up” rally.

💡 Conclusion
Put simply: sentiment is in greed while price is pulling back—this isn’t a breakdown scenario; it’s a cooling-off scenario. My view is very clear: defend in the short term, scale in during pullbacks; once the Greed Index washes back into the neutral zone, consider increasing position size again. According to CoinTelegraph, U.S. spot BTC ETFs have just sparked a rush of seven consecutive days of net inflows. The impact is very direct: the year-to-date net outflow gap since early 2026 has been cut by more than half.

Here’s where the progress bar stands now: this batch of funds is still $390 million short of the historical record for the single month of net inflows in October 2025. In other words, with another decent run of weekly inflows, the record could be tied—or even refreshed.

One-sentence translation: The Wall Street money that retreated in the first half of this year is queuing up to come back.

Market impact
Short term: Liquidity has clearly improved, but the price action hasn’t caught up yet—BTC is currently at $79,029.46 (24h -1.87%), ETH at $2,466.12 (-1.32%), while SOL and XRP are falling even harder, down more than 4%. ETF buy pressure and coin prices are temporarily diverging; this kind of divergence is usually resolved by the coin price catching up, not by another round of capital pullbacks.

Medium term: ETFs have shifted from being a “net outflow drag” to a “net inflow engine.” Narrative switching matters more than day-to-day inflows. If the gap turns positive and replicates the October 2025 rhythm, the institutional allocation logic can stand back on its feet.

My take
I’m moderately bullish. One reason: seven straight days of net inflows isn’t retail sentiment—it’s sustained institutional behavior, and it’s happening while the price is moving sideways and falling. Buying more as it dips—that structure is healthy.

On price: if BTC holds the $79,000 area, the divergence between ETF flows and the market is likely to converge upward. The risk is this: if next week’s inflows pause and flip to net outflows, the divergence logic would fail and the room for a pullback would reopen. Iran unilaterally announced that ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz require permission, which increases the oil price risk premium; negative risk-off sentiment is further intensifying.

Iran has publicly declared that it exercises control over the Strait of Hormuz and requires all vessels to obtain permission in advance. This strait is the most critical chokepoint for global oil transportation, through which about 20% of the world’s oil trade passes. In plain terms, this is not a military operation—it’s a political signaling move. Iran is telling the outside world: I have the ability to choke the lifeline of global energy. Escalation of regional tensions is almost inevitable.

Impact on the market
The transmission path is straightforward: Strait controlled → risk premium on oil prices rises → inflation expectations tick up → markets worry the Fed will find it harder to cut rates → pressure builds on risk assets.

- Medium term: If Iran really intercepts ships, oil prices could spike plus inflation could rebound, rate-cut expectations would effectively go to zero, and the medium-term valuation logic for crypto would be directly undermined.

My view
Bearish, but it’s a “risk-event-driven selloff,” not a trend reversal. On the daily timeframe, BTC has support around $76,000; only if it breaks below that level is there room for further downside. 当前1小时 -0.30%、24小时 -1.02%，两个周期没有形成足够清晰的同向配合。区间行情里，追涨杀跌的容错率较低，更适合用上沿确认方向、下沿确认承接，中轴只作为强弱分界。

1小时已经出现回踩，先看 2,414.64 是否形成稳定承接。价格若能快速收回 2,450.12，说明回撤仍可控；若反弹无力且低点继续下移，就不能再沿用强势逻辑。

我的推演不是单押一个方向。价格突破 2,485.6 且能保持，代表上方空间被重新打开；跌破 2,414.64 且反抽不过，代表结构进一步转弱；在两者之间运行，则继续观察 2,450.12 两侧的收盘情况。

对已有仓位的人，重点是按支撑是否失效来管理，而不是被每次波动带着走；对空仓的人，优先等待突破回踩或支撑确认。现货可以分批，合约则应缩短决策链条，先确定止损位置，再决定是否参与。

交易计划必须包含失效条件。判断正确可以分段兑现，判断错误也要允许自己退出，不能用加仓掩盖最初逻辑已经变化。行情会更新，观点也应跟随价格证据调整。

Within a week, ETH pulled up 28%. After it fell from 2533, it churned around 2450 for more than ten hours. In the order book, across 20 levels, the bid side is 12 times thicker than the ask side—looks like someone is propping it up. But in reality, the actual spot trades of active buying and selling are only 0.40, with sell pressure accounting for 60%. In the past three hours alone, net outflows totaled 41,000 ETH, and none of the twelve funding candles turned red. The support is a wall; the money is running out. I pick a side: short.

Both the derivatives side and on-chain data are confirming it. Open interest shrank by 2.62% in a day, the four-quadrant model called bear capitulation, and the basis turned negative—this isn’t longs retreating; they’re being liquidated. On-chain margin lending collapsed 94% over 12 hours. The ammunition for taking out loans and adding positions has already been used up. RSI is still sitting at an overbought 79.6. A 28% surge to this level was already due to “let some air out.”

Once that 2450 wall gets bitten through by sell orders, the first stop is the 2412 daily low. Below that is the 2355 three-day low. Leveraged longs are still crowding in at a 23:1 spot long/short ratio; when the level finally breaks, the snapback will be faster than the grinding we’ve seen.

When do I turn bullish? When spot flips back to net inflows over three hours, large orders turn to buys, OI starts adding back positions, or volume recovers and it reclaims 2475 and holds above 2533—then I’ll change my mind.
#eth $ETH

Bernstein sets three target price tiers: $125K is just the starting point—by 2029, it could reach $300K

Bernstein expects BTC to return to $125K by the end of 2026. Its baseline target is $300K in 2029, with a bull-case scenario of $500K.

Investment bank Bernstein has released its latest Bitcoin price forecast, with a clear three-tier roadmap. In the baseline case, BTC returns to $125,000 by the end of 2026 and reaches $300,000 by 2029; the optimistic case goes straight to $500,000. The key logic is that the peak of this cycle has not yet appeared—right now, the market is only in a mid-cycle pullback and consolidation. This is a rare, explicit pro-market call from a mainstream large bank during a period of market weakness; it’s not the kind of vague, “cautiously optimistic” stance.

Impact on the market
- Short term: BTC is currently at $78,381.15, down 0.69% over the past 24 hours. Such long-dated target prices have limited immediate effect on the order book, but they can provide a “the institution hasn’t bailed yet” anchor for sidelined observers and help suppress panic. ETH is at $2,459.76, moving in line with the broader market.
- Medium term: When big banks publicly provide a 2029 timeline, it effectively pulls Bitcoin’s long-term pricing power further into the traditional finance system. If more investment banks follow up by raising their targets, it will strengthen the narrative that “the cycle isn’t over,” potentially changing institutional allocation timing.

My take
I agree with the direction, but I’m cautious about the timeline. $125K implies there’s roughly 60% upside from today’s $78,381.15—this is not something that happens in just a couple of weeks. Two things to watch: first, whether the $75K support zone can hold; if it fails, Bernstein’s cycle thesis will need to be tested sooner. Second, the overhead resistance at $85K–$88K: only a breakout with strong volume would confirm the start of a new uptrend. Until then, this report looks more like “recharging confidence” for long-term holders—don’t treat it as a short-term instruction. The risk is that if macro liquidity tightens more than expected, the cycle-peak thesis could be disproven.

Why Does Bernstein Predict BTC Could Still Rise to $300,000 After Reaching $125,000 by Dec. 2026?

Wall Street investment bank Bernstein has spoken: BTC will reclaim $125,000 before the end of next year, reach $300,000 in 2029, and hit $500,000 in a bull-market scenario.

This Bernstein report lays out three tiers of forecasts: under the base case, BTC returns to $125,000 by the end of 2026, then surges to $300,000 in 2029; the optimistic case goes straight to $500,000. Pay attention to the wording—"reclaim," meaning to regain. In other words, they believe the current price around $78,381 is in the bottom-range of the cycle, and there is an entire new leg of the main uptrend ahead.

Since 2023, Bernstein has been one of the most steadfast BTC bulls on the Street—not the kind of analysts that just react to whatever the market is doing.

Impact on the market
- Short term: BTC is now $78,381 (24h -0.69%). These far-ahead target prices have limited direct impact on the current tape, but they give out-of-market investors a reference point—"the cycle top hasn’t arrived yet" in the institutional narrative. ETH $2,459 is moving sideways, and volume hasn’t picked up.
- Medium term: If the view that the cycle top in 2026 is already in focus becomes more widely adopted by institutions, the timing of ETF capital allocation could stretch out. Pullbacks may be treated as "buy-the-dip" windows rather than the end of a trend, and the volatility structure could become less sharp.

My take
I agree with the direction, but the timing is questionable. With $78,381 currently, there’s about 60% room to $125,000. You can’t get there based on a single report—you need a liquidity backdrop to cooperate. For now, watch whether BTC can hold the $80,000 level; below that, $75,000 is the make-or-break support for this move. Put simply: being bullish on the long term doesn’t mean it will go up right now. The interim drawdowns could get so deep that most people won’t be able to hold.

One-sentence translation: The bank says this is only a relay station—but the road from the relay station to the finish has never been a straight line.

title: السوق الهابطة انتهت؟ دعنا نقرأ ما تقوله الأرقام الحقيقية
subTitle:
من الخوف إلى الطمع في 14 يومًا فقط

في 12 أغسطس، كان مؤشر الخوف والطمع عند 27 — "خوف شديد".

الأمس، وصل إلى 74 — "طمع". واليوم، استقر عند 65.

في أقل من أسبوعين، تحول السوق من الذعر الجماعي إلى التفاؤل. هذا ليس مجرد تغير في المزاج — هذا تحول هيكلي في نفسية السوق.

والمفارقة؟ نفس الأشخاص الذين كانوا خائفين من الشراء عند 68 ألف دولار، هم الآن خائفون من تفويت الفرصة عند 80 ألف دولار.
الأرقام التي لا تكذب: ثلاث قصص متوازية
القصة الأولى: Bitcoin $BTC — أقوى انتعاش في 12 شهرًا

بيتكوين لم تعد مجرد "ترتد". إنها تتقدم.

وفقًا لبيانات CryptoQuant، ارتفع مؤشر "القراءة الصاعدة" من 30 إلى 80 في 7 أيام فقط — 8 من 10 مؤشرات فرعية تحولت إلى المنطقة الإيجابية.

هذه هي أسرع وتيرة صاعدة خلال الـ 12 شهرًا الماضية.

السعر لامس 81,272 دولارًا، وهو الأعلى منذ 15 مايو 2026. صحيح أنه تراجع إلى حوالي 78,500-79,000 دولار，لكن هذا التراجع طبيعي. بعد قفزة 24% في أيام قليلة，أي سوق يحتاج إلى تنفس.

الأهم: بيتكوين صامدة فوق المتوسطات المتحركة لـ 20 و50 و200 يوم — هيكل اتجاه صاعد قيد التكوين.

القصة الثانية: Ethereum — اختراق بعد جمود طويل

إيثريوم كسرت أخيرًا النطاق العرضي الطويل. السعر الآن حول 2,440-2,480 دولارًا，بعد أن كانت تتداول حول 1,870-1,920 دولارًا قبل أسبوعين فقط.

المؤشرات الفنية تتحدث بوضوح: جميع المتوسطات المتحركة انقلبت إلى الأعلى، MACD في تقاطع ذهبي مع امتداد للون الأحمر. حتى لو حدث تصحيح قصير الأجل — وهذا متوقع بعد هذا الصعود السريع — فإن الهيكل الصاعد على المدى المتوسط لا يزال سليمًا طالما بقي السعر فوق 2,242 دولارًا.

الأهم من ذلك: إيثريوم تستعد لأكبر ترقية بروتوكولية منذ "الدمج" — Glamsterdam. الاختبارات العامة بدأت بالفعل في 20 أغسطس. الترقيات الكبرى تاريخيًا كانت محفزات صاعدة لهذا الأصل.

القصة الثالثة: Solana $SOL  — انفجار على كل المستويات

سولانا سجلت 13.2 مليار معاملة غير تصويتية في أسبوع واحد — رقم قياسي تاريخي. عدد حاملي الأصول الواقعية (RWA) على شبكتها تجاوز 300 ألف، وإجمالي القيمة المحجوزة في DeFi ارتفع إلى 10.7 مليار دولار.

هذا ليس مجرد ارتفاع سعري. هذه شبكة تنبض بالحياة.

صحيح أن SOL تراجعت من 100 دولار إلى حوالي 97 دولارًا، لكنها قفزت من 60 دولارًا في يونيو — نسبة ارتفاع تتجاوز 60%.
ما يحدث تحت السطح: قصة المؤسسات

هنا تكمن المعلومة الحصرية التي لا تتحدث عنها الشموع:

صناديق Bitcoin و Ethereum $ETH المتداولة (ETFs) سجلت 453 مليون دولار من التدفقات الداخلة في يوم واحد، لتمتد بذلك سلسلة التدفقات الإيجابية إلى 6 أيام متتالية.

في الأسبوع الماضي وحده، اجتذبت صناديق ETFs الأمريكية للعملات الرقمية 2.71 مليار دولار — أقوى أداء أسبوعي منذ أكتوبر 2025.

بلاك روك، أكبر مدير أصول في العالم (يدير 15.3 تريليون دولار)، قاد التدفقات بـ 209 ملايين دولار لصناديق Bitcoin و 90.9 مليون دولار لصناديق Ethereum في يوم واحد.

أما بالنسبة لسولانا، فقد شهدت صناديقها المتداولة 3350 مليون دولار من التدفقات في يوم واحد — وهو أعلى مستوى يومي على الإطلاق، ليرتفع إجمالي التدفقات إلى 1.22 مليار دولار. عملاء Bitwise اشتروا سولانا لـ 5 أيام متتالية بقيمة إجمالية تقارب 950 مليون دولار.

المؤسسات لا تشتري بدافع العاطفة. تشتري عندما ترى القيمة.

---

ماذا يقول لنا التاريخ؟

آخر مرة كان فيها مؤشر الخوف والطمع عند هذا المستوى (74) كانت في 5 أكتوبر 2025. بعدها بخمسة أيام فقط، حدثت أكبر موجة تصفية في تاريخ العملات الرقمية — 19 مليار دولار.

لكن: في ذلك الوقت، كانت بيتكوين تتداول عند حوالي 124,000 دولار. واليوم، نحن عند 78,500 دولار. السوق مختلف، السياق مختلف، والمحفزات مختلفة.

اليوم، لدينا:

· تحفيز نقدي من خزانة الأمريكية — برنامج إعادة شراء السندات طويلة الأجل بقيمة لا تقل عن 40 مليار دولار شهريًا
· دعم سياسي واضح من البيت الأبيض
· سيولة مؤسسية تعود بقوة
· نشاط شبكي يسجل أرقامًا قياسية
الاستنتاج المتفائل المدعوم بالأرقام

المرحلة الأكثر قسوة في السوق الهابط انتهت. هذا ليس رأيًا، هذه قراءة للبيانات.

لكن السوق الصاعد الجديد لم يحصل بعد على التأكيد النهائي — وهذا ليس تشاؤمًا، هذه دعوة للانضباط.

الفرق الآن هو أن الأساسيات تغيرت. لم نعد في سوق يعتمد على المضاربة وحدها. نحن في سوق حيث:

· المؤسسات تشتري
· الشبكات تنمو
· السياسات تدعم
· السيولة تتدفق

المخاطرة الآن ليست في تفويت القاع. المخاطرة في انتظار تأكيد لا يأتي إلا بعد فوات الأوان.

title: ⚠️ Estrategia 3-2-1 para operar la volatilidad actual sin quemar tu cuenta
subTitle:
El mercado está mostrando movimientos falsos en zonas clave y muchos traders están cayendo en trampas de liquidez por entrar en FOMO. Si quieres proteger tu capital y capturar movimientos de BTCyETH con gestión de riesgo real, aplica esta regla de 3 pasos:
1. No entres al rompimiento, espera la confirmación
El 70% de los rompimientos en niveles de resistencia clave terminan siendo "fakeouts" (falsas rupturas).
Qué hacer: Deja que el precio rompa, espera el retest al nivel roto como soporte y busca un patrón de vela de reversión (como martillo o envolvente) en temporalidad de 15m o 1h.
2. Define tu Invalidación (Stop Loss) ANTES de calcular el beneficio
Nunca entres a una posición calculando cuánto vas a ganar sin saber cuánto vas a arriesgar.
Fórmula rápida: Arriesga máximo el 1% al 2% de tu capital total por operación.Si tu cuenta es de $100 USDT, tu pérdida máxima por operación no debería superar los $2 USDT. Ajusta el apalancamiento y el tamaño de posición en función de la distancia a tu Stop Loss, no al revés.
3. Configura DCA automático o Grilla (Grid Trading) en zonas de consolidación
Si no tienes tiempo para estar pegado a la pantalla todo el día, los bots de Spot Grid en Binance funcionan excelente en rangos laterales.
Configura un rango entre el soporte principal del gráfico diario y la resistencia más cercana.Permite que el bot ejecute compras en caídas y ventas en repuntes automáticamente.

BNB Chain’s August 25 hard fork: Why it’s said to be “relieving” the ecosystem?

BNB Chain’s Pasteur hard fork is scheduled for mainnet activation on August 25, directly impacting BNB holders and on-chain developers.

BNB Chain has officially confirmed that the Pasteur hard fork will go live on the mainnet on August 25. In plain terms, it’s a systematic upgrade to the chain—mainly aimed at reducing network load and optimizing on-chain performance—so that developers and validating nodes can run with fewer resources. This kind of upgrade doesn’t create new coins and doesn’t involve a transfer fork. BNB holders don’t need to do anything. However, after the upgrade, the chain’s throughput and fee structure will change, and ecosystem projects will be the most direct beneficiaries.

One-sentence translation: The chain’s foundation has been refurbished—nothing obvious in the short term, but building on it will be more stable going forward.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Before the upgrade, there’s usually narrative-driven speculation. Today, BNB is up 0.81% over the last 24 hours, trading at $702.18—one of the few major coins in the green (BTC $78,486.93 down 0.75%, ETH $2,461.59 down 0.76%). Funds are leaning toward certainty-driven events amid weakness.
- Medium term: After the upgrade is兑现ed, narrative heat will cool. BNB’s core support still depends on the Binance platform token aspect and on-chain activity. The hard fork itself doesn’t change the valuation logic.

My view
I’m neutral-to-bullish, but I only provide this for the period leading up to the event’s兑现. Before August 25, BNB has a clear time anchor, and in a weak market the chance of an independent move isn’t low. If the $700 level holds, there’s still upside momentum. But note: the day the upgrade is deployed could be a “good news is already priced in” node, and the price may not necessarily give it credit. With the broader market like this, a single-chain upgrade can’t drive the whole market’s rhythm.

BNB Chain 8月25日硬分叉，为何说是为生态减负？

BNB Chain的Pasteur硬分叉定档8月25日主网激活，直接影响BNB持有者和链上开发者。

BNB Chain官方确认，Pasteur硬分叉将在8月25日上线主网。说白了就是给链做一次系统性升级，主要方向是降低网络运行负担、优化链上性能，让开发者和验证节点跑起来更省资源。这类升级不产生新币、不涉及转账分叉，BNB持有者不需要做任何操作，但升级后链的吞吐和费用结构会变，生态项目方是最直接的受益者。

一句话翻译：链的底座翻新了，短期看不太出来，但以后在上面盖楼更稳。

对市场的影响
- 短期：升级前通常有叙事炒作，BNB今天24h +0.81%，报$702.18，是主流币里少数翻红的（BTC $78,486.93跌0.75%，ETH $2,461.59跌0.76%）。资金在弱势里往确定性事件靠。
- 中期：升级兑现后叙事热度会衰减，BNB的核心支撑还是看币安平台币的属性和链上活跃度，硬分叉本身不改变估值逻辑。

我的判断
我观点是中性偏多，但只给到事件兑现前这一段。8月25日之前BNB有明确的时间锚，弱势行情里有独立行情的概率不低；$700这个位置守住了，上探动能还在。但要注意升级落地当天可能是“利好兑现”节点，价格反而不一定给面子。大盘这个样子，单一链升级带不动整个市场节奏。

If it holds, you earn the right to look back for a rebound toward 79,194; if it breaks, downside room will keep opening—don’t fantasize about an immediate V-reversal. Oh my! 262%! This BTR move totally stunned me—pumped from 0.029 to 0.125, and it more than tripled in a day. Getting #1 on the trending list is definitely not just for show. Honestly, I didn’t expect Bitlayer, this long-standing BTC Layer 2, to be this wild. Trading volume has surged to 3.8x the average—an $551M trading value is absolutely insane (but still makes sense) in the current market.

Hold up—don’t rush in to chase, friends. I checked: BTR’s current price at 0.1196 is already at about 94% of its 24h range. It’s only a breath away from the high of 0.1255. The funding rate is 0.085%, and longs are getting a bit overheated. At this position, if you want in, honestly it’s much more comfortable to wait for a pullback rather than buy the spike. My short-term idea is: if the pullback to around 0.10–0.105 holds up, you can consider a mildly bullish bias. Stop-loss at 0.092 (if it breaks below the previous candle body’s low, I’d call it wrong and exit). First target is the previous high near 0.125—risk/reward about 1:2.5, not bad. But pay attention: if it breaks below 0.092 and volume increases, it likely means the rally’s chips are being distributed—run quickly, don’t get stubborn.

For the mid-term, we need to see whether it can hold above 0.08 before taking a deeper position. Right now, to be real, the spot feels a bit awkward—chasing in can easily get you washed.

TAC is also flying today: +72%, price at 0.0040, and it’s at 88% of its range. Volume is 1.2x average volume—not as crazy as BTR, and it’s moving relatively healthily. The funding rate is 0.0263%, which is normal and shows no overheating signal. I think this setup is worth watching for a pullback to the 0.0035–0.0036 support area. Stop-loss at 0.0033, target 0.0043, RR also around 1:2.5. But TAC’s problem is that its market cap is too small and liquidity is average—don’t be too heavy on position sizing. I’ve been burned on small coins like this before (don’t ask how I know—too much talk turns into tears).

BMT is interesting: +59%, but funding rate is -0.31%—a bunch of shorts got squeezed. This combination of negative funding plus a rise often means shorts are hard holding; once price breaks above the resistance at 0.0272, short stop-losses may actually fuel the move. Current price is 0.0245, leaving about ~10% upside before the resistance. If you want to trade it, entering after the break above 0.0272 is safer, with stop-loss at 0.0248 and target 0.032. RR roughly 1:1.8. But note: BMT spiked to 0.02782 today and then pulled back, leaving an upper wick—suggesting sell pressure overhead. Chasing here can be risky.

As for the broader market: BTC is ranging around 78.5K—up 22% over 7 days. ETH is even stronger, up 28.7%. Fear & Greed Index is 50—neutral, slightly hesitant. A classic “up but too scared to chase, down but too scared to buy” kind of state. I think in this environment, altcoin momentum will likely continue, but differentiation will increase. The coins near the top of the gainers list are either driven by strong narratives or backed by real volume. Avoid the ones that are just hopping on the hype.

Oh—and on the losers list: SCRT -24%, STORJ -20%. These early movers that ran up too much? Their pullbacks also won’t be logical. I’ve taken this kind of loss before: when it was pumping I didn’t catch it, but when it dropped I nailed the bottom like a perfect bag-holder (manual dog-head).

To sum up my stance: if the broader market holds up, altcoins stay active, but sentiment is neutral. It’s suitable for light position trial-and-error, not for going all-in with heavy size. For BTR, look for a pullback; for TAC, watch pullback support; for BMT, wait for breakout confirmation. Remember: every idea needs a stop-loss—don’t let one mistake wipe out the money you earned from ten correct trades.

大盘方面，BTC在78.5K附近震荡，7天涨了22%，ETH更猛，28.7%。恐惧贪婪指数50，中性偏犹豫，典型的"涨了不敢追，跌了不敢买"的状态。我觉得这种环境下，山寨币的行情大概率还会延续，但分化会加剧。涨幅榜前排的币要么是强叙事，要么是有真实量能支撑，那些跟风蹭热度的千万别碰。

哦对了，跌幅榜上SCRT -24%、STORJ -20%，这种前期涨太多的，回调起来也是不讲道理的。我之前就吃过这种亏，涨的时候没赶上，跌的时候倒是精准接盘（手动狗头）。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  I took a careful look at Citadel 2 by @Dusk_Foundation  recently. Their pitch of “single authentication, permanent access” is definitely catchy—after all, everyone is sick of repeatedly sending passports back and forth. The operating logic seems pretty smooth: users find an authorized node (LP), complete an offline review, and obtain an encrypted credential on-chain. When dealing with various service providers (SP), users only need to prove compliance via ZK, with zero privacy leakage. Paired with a “market view” of about 0.074 USD for $DUSK , there’s a lot of room for this narrative. But digging into the details shows that the vision still needs more runway before it can really land.

The biggest pitfall is the “trust gap.” The documentation is explicit: who’s accepted and whose LP account gets recognized—entirely depends on the SP. That’s awkward: suppose an exchange like NPEX only recognizes Institution A, while a certain DeFi project trusts Institution B instead. In that case, users still have to redo the review. Before broad cross-application mutual recognition becomes a real norm, the so-called “network-wide compatibility” is really just self-entertainment within the influence sphere of a single service provider. #dusk

Infrastructure progress is also lagging. At this point, which mature institutions have actually managed to run nodes end-to-end? I scoured the official code repositories and found that the JavaScript SDK for B-side integration is still hanging with a “please stay tuned” label. The only usable zk-citadel-wallet available right now is a command-line tool meant for developer testing. For traditional institutions, without a complete development package to force the integration, the cost of stumbling around is far higher than simply buying an off-the-shelf Web2 solution.

Compared with Europe’s traditional identity framework like eIDAS, Citadel’s privacy protection is indeed ahead. But its “commercial consensus network” is too thin. In short: the underlying framework is fine, but network effects still have to be built over time. I’m currently watching two indicators: first, when truly licensed institutions will step in as LPs; second, when the JS SDK will finally be delivered for commercial use. Until then, “one-time KYC” is more like a catchy gimmick—it’s still a long way from becoming a truly usable, nationwide product. #eth $ETH

Samsung Electronics and SK hynix see intraday high gains narrow at the close

On August 26, major Asia-Pacific stock indexes closed broadly stronger overall. South Korea’s KOSPI closed up 0.97% at 6808.21. Market attention focused on two leading Korean memory-chip companies: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. Both stocks rose during the day with intraday gains peaking above 3%, but then suddenly pulled back at the close; their closing gains narrowed to 1.75% and 0.6%, respectively. On the same day, Japan’s Nikkei 225 closed up 0.62% at 66,262.16, while memory-chip-related company Kioxia fell 2.46% and SoftBank Group rose 1.49%. Against the backdrop of most major Asia-Pacific indexes closing higher, the “two memory bellwethers” shifted from intraday strength to a clearly smaller gain at the close, becoming the standout change in that day’s intraday structure.

As for the background, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are core suppliers on the global memory-chip supply side, and their stock-price fluctuations are often used to gauge expectations for the semiconductor cycle and investors’ risk appetite for Asian tech stocks. Even though the Korean composite index still logged close to a 1% gain, this suggests the broader market did not weaken in tandem. What truly drew attention was the rhythm shift in the memory leaders in the late-session period—gains of more than 3% during the day failed to fully hold through to the close. Public reporting provides the closing results compared with the intraday highs, but does not simultaneously disclose any specific sudden company announcements or policy information sufficient to independently explain the late-session pullback; therefore, conclusions about the cause must remain restrained.

The core facts can be summarized in three points. First, the KOSPI closed higher and the broader pattern of collective gains across major Asia-Pacific indexes was in place. Second, the intraday peak gains for Samsung Electronics and SK hynix both exceeded 3%, indicating there was still upward momentum from the morning through the afternoon. Third, both stocks fell quickly in the late session, ultimately closing up 1.75% and 0.6% respectively—meaning their gains narrowed significantly versus their intraday highs. In Japan, Kioxia closed lower while SoftBank Group closed higher, so memory-related names internally were not consistent. Interpreting “a late-session pullback” as “a switch from gains to losses” is inaccurate, because both companies still ended the day with positive returns; the change is mainly reflected in the narrowing of gains and weaker intraday performance late in the day.

In terms of logic, intraday spikes are often driven by short-term buying pressure or a rising mood in the sector; a sudden narrowing of gains late in the session is more commonly seen when profit-taking crystallizes, liquidity thins near the close, or investors become more cautious about overnight overseas markets and the expectations for the next day’s open. Since existing materials do not provide a single clear news catalyst, the more cautious explanation is that this was a rhythm adjustment occurring within an up day, rather than a confirmed turning point in fundamentals. Memory-chip stock prices often carry both long-term supply–demand narratives and short-term capital-market games, and these two should not be conflated. Turning a late-session intraday fluctuation directly into an industry-cycle reversal is over-extrapolation. Similarly, ignoring the pullback strength simply because the stocks still rose at the close would also underestimate the informational value of short-term volatility itself.

The impact path on the crypto market is mainly indirect transmission of risk appetite, not a deterministic correlation with any specific token. The intraday strength and weakness of Asian semiconductor and tech leaders is sometimes used by certain market participants as an observation window for global growth-stock sentiment and the “temperature” of high-volatility risk assets. When memory leaders see a spike followed by a pullback, short-term traders may simultaneously reassess their willingness to chase risk assets higher. Digital assets—being part of the global risk-asset complex—are sometimes affected by this kind of sentiment spillover. However, this path is not stable and is constrained by factors such as macro liquidity, the dollar environment, leverage within the crypto market, and trading/transaction structure. Therefore, the narrowing of late-session gains in Korean memory stocks is better viewed as one slice of Asia-Pacific tech risk sentiment, rather than a direct guiding signal for crypto price action.

The editorial view is: the more important information that day was not a “collapse in memory stocks,” but rather “strong stocks giving up part of their intraday profits at the close.” Both the KOSPI and the Nikkei 225 still closed up, suggesting the regional market’s main trend remained relatively positive. The memory duo’s closing strength also indicates that selling pressure had not yet pushed prices back to flat or turned them negative. Future monitoring should continue to distinguish facts from speculation: verified is the gap between the August 26 intraday high and the closing gain; not yet verified is whether the late-session pullback was triggered by specific supply–demand data, order expectations, or mapped moves from overseas markets. For readers interested in tech narratives and cross-market sentiment involving digital assets, this kind of intraday structure from leading companies can be treated as a sentiment reference—but it should not be used to derive a medium-term trend from a single day’s late-session volatility, nor should it be simplified into a one-directional up-or-down conclusion.

三星电子与SK海力士盘中冲高尾盘涨幅收窄

8月26日，亚太主要股指收盘整体偏强。韩国综合指数收盘上涨0.97%，报6808.21点。市场焦点集中在韩国两家存储芯片龙头三星电子与SK海力士：两股当日震荡上行，盘中最高涨幅均超过3%，但尾盘突然回落，收盘涨幅分别收窄至1.75%与0.6%。同日，日经225指数收盘上涨0.62%，报66262.16点；存储芯片相关企业铠侠下跌2.46%，软银集团上涨1.49%。在亚太主要指数多数收红的背景下，韩国存储双雄由盘中强势转为尾盘涨幅明显收敛，成为当日分时结构上的突出变化。

事件背景上，三星电子与SK海力士是全球存储芯片供给端的核心厂商，其股价波动常被用来观察半导体景气预期与亚洲科技股风险偏好。当日韩国综指仍录得接近一个百分点的上涨，说明大盘层面并未同步转弱；真正引起注意的，是存储龙头在尾盘阶段的节奏切换，即盘中超过3%的冲高未能完整保留到收盘。公开报道给出的是收盘结果与盘中高点对比，并未同步披露足以单独解释尾盘回落的突发公司公告或政策信息，因此对原因的判断必须克制。

核心事实可以概括为三点。第一，韩国综指收涨，亚太主要股指集体上涨的格局成立。第二，三星电子、SK海力士盘中最高涨幅均超过3%，显示早盘至午后仍有上攻动能。第三，尾盘两股快速回落，最终分别以1.75%、0.6%收盘，涨幅较盘中高点明显收窄；日本市场中铠侠收跌、软银收涨，存储相关标的内部并不一致。把“尾盘回落”理解成“由涨转跌”并不准确，因为两家公司收盘仍为正收益，变化主要体现在涨幅收敛与分时走弱。

逻辑拆解上，盘中冲高通常对应短线买盘推动或板块情绪升温；尾盘突然收窄，则更常见于获利盘兑现、流动性在临近收市时变薄，或对隔夜外盘与隔日开盘预期趋于谨慎。由于现有材料没有给出单一明确的消息催化，更稳妥的解释是：这是一场发生在上行日内部的节奏调整，而不是已经被证实的基本面拐点。存储芯片股价往往同时承载中长期供需叙事与短期资金博弈，二者不能混为一谈。把尾盘分时波动直接上升为行业周期反转，属于过度外推；同样，因为收盘仍上涨就完全忽视回落力度，也会低估短线波动本身的信息含量。

对加密市场的影响路径，主要是间接的风险偏好传导，而非映射到某一特定代币的确定性联动。亚洲半导体与科技龙头的分时强弱，常被部分市场参与者当作全球成长股情绪与高波动风险资产温度的观察窗口。当存储龙头出现冲高回落时，短线交易者可能同步重新评估风险资产的追涨意愿；数字资产作为全球风险资产谱系的一部分，有时会受到这类情绪外溢影响。但这一路径并不稳定，还受到宏观流动性、美元环境、加密市场自身杠杆与成交结构等因素制约。因此，韩股存储股尾盘涨幅收窄，更适合被视为亚太科技风险情绪的一个切片，而不是加密行情的直接指引信号。

编辑判断是：当日更关键的信息不是“存储股崩溃”，而是“强势股在尾盘交出部分盘中利润”。韩国综指与日经225仍收涨，说明区域市场主线仍偏积极；存储双雄收盘维持上涨，也表明抛压尚未把价格打回平盘或翻绿。后续观察应继续区分事实与推测：已核实的是8月26日盘中高点与收盘涨幅的落差；尚未核实的是尾盘回落是否由特定供需数据、订单预期或外盘映射触发。对关注科技叙事与数字资产交叉情绪的读者而言，可以把此类龙头分时结构当作情绪参考，但应避免由单一交易日尾盘波动推导中期趋势，更不宜将其简化为单向涨跌结论。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  After long-term tracking @Dusk, my focus long ago shifted from “whether RWA works” to a more grounded existential question: when the business finally lands, how will the benefits be effectively transmitted to $DUSK?

Objectively speaking, the website’s data is impressive: it confirms an issuance size of over €300 million, reaches more than 50,000 investors, and the staked amount has also surpassed 210 million DUSK. On top of that, the team is aggressively pushing NPEX, the SME private placement market, and Dusk Trade—this compliant on-chain framework. The business narrative is already quite complete.

But the moment you look at the token model, that sense of fracture shows up. Right now, DUSK’s core consumption scenarios are still centered on running nodes and paying gas. Referencing on-chain data from August 23, the total staked across the network is about 215.6 million tokens, and the APR can still stay around 22%. The problem is: this such high payout isn’t funded by real business cashflows; the system still needs to unlock as many as 500 million tokens over the next 36 years.

That’s incredibly awkward. The ultra-high returns you see today are essentially propped up by “printing for the future” to keep today’s large lockers in place. If they try to keep this logic going, in the end it will definitely rely on massive real network transaction fees to absorb the demand. And that’s what baffles me the most: putting a €300 million traditional asset on-chain sounds huge, but that so-called “asset size” absolutely does not equal the actual buying demand of $DUSK .

How high is the turnover rate of these regulated allocations? How much gas can they realistically burn? Are those meager pass-through fees enough to offset the dilution effects caused by inflation? Ordinary retail investors can’t even figure these things out.

And even if transaction fees make it into the pool, they’re still distributed to validators and funds—there isn’t even a complete burn mechanism.

So my doubts about Dusk are not that it hasn’t been doing things. It’s that, even if the work gets done, the token may not necessarily absorb any “blood.” Stop obsessing over those partnership press releases worth a few hundred million. What we should relentlessly focus on is: how much real on-chain consumption can this batch of assets generate each month without relying on inflation subsidies. This set of hard data is the only criterion to test valuation. #eth $ETH

这就非常尴尬了。眼前的超高回报，骨子里是用“未来印钞”来稳住现在的锁仓大户。这套逻辑想一直玩下去，最后绝对得靠海量的真实网络手续费来接盘。这也是我最纳闷的地方：3 亿欧元传统标的搬上链听着是很庞大，但这所谓的“资产体量”绝对不等于 $DUSK 的“实际买盘”。

这些受监管份额到底有多高的换手率？能烧掉多少 Gas？微薄的过路费究竟够不够填补通胀带来的稀释效应？普通散户根本算不明白。况且交易费进池子后，还是分给验证者和基金，连个彻底的销毁机制都没有。

所以，我现在对 Dusk 的疑虑不在于它没做事，而是事做成了，代币却未必能吸到血。以后别老盯着那些几个亿的合作通稿了，咱们该死死盯住的，是这批资产每个月究竟能逼出多少不靠通胀补贴的真实链上消耗。这组干货数据，才是检验估值的唯一标准。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  I’ve been thinking about @Dusk lately, and I’ve realized that what I care about most isn’t whether the “RWA track” can succeed, but a very practical question: once the asset side really grows big, what exactly will the resulting benefits be used to pay back to $DUSK?

There’s no denying the impressive scoreboard shown on the official website: over €300 million in confirmed issuance, attracting 50,000+ investors, plus more than 210 million staked tokens. And with the recent official hard push on NPEX, the SME private placement market, and the Dusk Trade compliant on-chain system, the business map is clearly getting sturdier.

However, when I shift my focus back to the token model, a strong sense of disconnect comes over me. For now, DUSK’s core spending/consumption path is still limited to gas fees and node lockups. Looking at third-party data from August 23rd, the total staked amount across the network is about 215.6 million tokens, and the APR is still holding around 22%. But this rich distribution isn’t backed by real commercial profit. After all, the network will still need to release up to 500 million tokens over the next 36 years.

That’s where things get awkward. High returns right now are, in the end, like “borrowing tomorrow’s inflationary share to pay today’s wages.” If this is going to work long-term, the only way out is to rely on real, on-chain network usage fees to cover the bill.

And that’s exactly what bothers me most: moving €300 million in traditional assets onto the chain sounds impressive, but that huge “capital volume” must absolutely not be substituted for the actual buy-side demand of $DUSK . We need to think carefully—how many genuinely active trades can these regulated allocations translate into? How much gas will they burn? And those modest toll fees: how much of the selling pressure created by new issuance can they actually offset? For ordinary token holders, this is basically an accounting problem you can’t even make sense of. What’s more, once these fees go into the block rewards pool, they’re ultimately distributed proportionally to nodes and the foundation—there’s no simple, brutal token-burn deflation mechanism.

My biggest sticking point with Dusk isn’t that they can’t build products. It’s that as the business wheels are already turning, the token still hasn’t demonstrated a strong, self-sustaining token-capture loop. Going forward, those “RWA strategy” PR victories running into the hundreds of millions can be set aside for now.

title: A Cheap Price Doesn't Always Mean a Cheap Asset.
subTitle:
One of the easiest mistakes in investing is assuming: "The price is low, therefore it's a bargain." Not necessarily. A token trading at $0.001 isn't automatically cheaper than one trading at $100.
The price of a single token tells us very little by itself. We need to look deeper:
🔹 Market capitalization
🔹 Token supply
🔹 Token utility
🔹 Adoption and demand
🔹 Revenue or network activity, where applicable
🔹 Development and ecosystem
🔹 Competition
🔹 Risks and sustainability
A low unit price can create the illusion of affordability. But what matters is not simply how much one token costs. What matters is what you're actually getting for your capital.
🔑 Key Takeaway: Never confuse a low token price with low valuation. A $0.001 token can be extremely expensive. A $100 asset can potentially be undervalued. The number on the price screen is only the beginning of the analysis.
🧠 Practical Reflection; Before buying a low-priced token, ask: "Am I attracted to this project because its fundamentals make sense or simply because the number looks small?" That one question can prevent a lot of emotional decisions.
Thought for the Day. Don't ask only, "How much is one coin? Ask: "What am I actually buying, and what gives it value?"
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

Bernstein sets new goals for BTC: $150K by 2027, $300K by 2029—why? 
Bernstein’s research note is bullish on BTC: $150K in mid-2027, $300K in 2029. The core logic is that institutions will use “adding currency while debasing it.”

Investment bank Bernstein has released a new Bitcoin price forecast with a very clear timeline: it expects $150,000 by mid-2027 and $300,000 in 2029. The current price is $78,442, meaning BTC would need to rise by about 91% by mid-2027 and about 282% by 2029.

Their case hinges on just two points: first, sustained institutional inflows (ETFs, corporate allocations); second, demand to hedge against the long-term depreciation of fiat currency. These two drivers are meant to shift Bitcoin from a speculative asset toward a more mature one—lower volatility, weaker cyclical effects, and a move higher in the valuation center of gravity.

Impact on the market
- Short term: the research note itself doesn’t directly pull in new buy orders, but it gives institutional investors a reason to allocate capital, indirectly supporting BTC’s price. With BTC currently at $78,442 (24h -1.07%), it’s in a consolidation range; reports like this reinforce the consensus that “a pullback is an opportunity.”
- Medium term: if institutions follow through on this logic, ETF inflows should keep lifting BTC’s bottom. Bernstein’s view carries an implicit premise: volatility convergence. In other words, the drawdown size in each future cycle may become smaller over time—an over-structure positive for long-term holders.

My take
I’m clearly bullish on the direction. The transmission path is very specific: institutional capital → net ETF inflows → directly absorbing BTC’s circulating supply → the price valuation center moves higher. This route has already been proven once over the past two years.

But pay attention to the time horizon. $150K is a target for mid-2027, not something for tomorrow. In the short term, BTC is around the $78K area. Moody’s Upgrades Coinbase Rating to B1: Cash Piles Higher Than Debt—Will Institutions Move In?

Moody’s has raised Coinbase’s credit rating to B1 with a stable outlook, easing another concern for institutional capital entering the market.

In this move, Moody’s upgraded Coinbase from the junk category up to B1. The core logic is simple: the company’s cash on hand far exceeds its debt level. In plain terms, this exchange isn’t short on money, and the risk of bankruptcy and default is declining. Credit-rating agencies rarely touch crypto companies, and granting a “stable outlook” is effectively an indirect endorsement of the industry’s corporate creditworthiness. For Coinbase, the cost of financing should fall, and when talking to institutions about custody services and wholesale brokerage, it can stand a firmer ground.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Sentiment is a positive, but don’t expect the COIN rating upgrade to directly pump BTC. BTC is $78,035.55 (-1.83% over 24 hours), ETH is $2,450.95 (-1.29%). Overall, the market is still in a low-volume, downward drift—one credit event can’t shake the broader market.
- Medium term: This is the real focus. Institutional allocation to crypto comes with a long compliance checklist, and counterparty risk from exchanges is one item. A rating upgrade means another box gets checked off. Over the long run, it helps pave the way for over-the-counter capital. If S&P and Fitch follow next, the industry’s credit framework will gradually take shape.

My take
I’m bullish on the direction, but the timing needs to be realistic: BTC is building a base around $78,000, and XRP’s -7% drop-style move shows that market risk appetite hasn’t fully returned. In the short run, credit positives may get drowned out by broader market sentiment. Over the medium term, this signal is more solid than most pieces of news—rating agencies calculate defaults using real, hard models, not just “being bullish” with words. If BTC can hold above $78,000 within the next 12 hours, the positive catalysts will slowly be priced in.

316.5%! BTR directly blew my mind. In one day it went from 0.029 to 0.146 and then pulled back to 0.138; the volume hit $840 million, which is 1.6x its usual average volume. Honestly, when I saw it this morning I thought the data was wrong. I rubbed my eyes and checked again… Alright, unbelievable but makes sense. After all, the BitVM narrative has been building heat for these past few months, and today is one of those concentrated breakout days.

Let me first talk about a detail I noticed: BTR’s current price is 0.138, about 5% away from the 24h high of 0.146, but the funding rate is already at 0.0998%. That number is extremely outrageous. What does it mean? It means the long side in the perpetual contract market has crowded into a tight spot—everyone is betting it will keep rising. In that kind of situation, I actually feel calmer, because an excessively high positive funding rate often means the fuel for a short squeeze has basically burned out, and a long liquidation cascade could happen at any moment. I’m not saying it will definitely drop, but chasing at this level really doesn’t offer a good risk-reward.

If I had to give a short-term plan, I personally would lean toward waiting for a pullback. At the current 0.138 level, 0.146 overhead is a hard resistance. The nearest support below is 0.07714. The space between them is huge—so if it does pull back, the move could be quite deep. For a long entry reference, I think the 0.10–0.11 range could work. Put the stop-loss at 0.085, and the first target would be 0.146. Let’s calculate the risk-reward: roughly 1:1.5. To be honest, that’s not especially enticing. But if the price breaks above 0.146 with strong volume and holds, then it’s a different story—at that point the odds of the breakout would be much higher. The invalidation conditions are very clear: if the next 4-hour candles close below 0.10 and the trading volume continues to expand, it means the follow-through on this pump isn’t strong enough, and the short-term long thesis is basically dead.

Now ONG—this one surprises me a bit. Ontology’s long-established token is up +60% today, volume is 3x the average, but the funding rate is -1.4995%—shorts are overheated. This is a very interesting signal. A negative funding rate means a bunch of people in the contract market are positioned for it to fall, but the price is being violently pushed up. Usually that implies shorts are being squeezed. The 24h low is 0.07288, and now it’s 0.1619—positioned at 75% of the range. Resistance is at 0.1878. For a short-term idea, I think this negative funding rate actually provides support for a long-leaning view. Entry reference would be around 0.15, stop-loss at 0.128, first target 0.1878, and the risk-reward is around 1:1.8. Invalidation: if price breaks below 0.128 and the funding rate flips positive quickly, it means the shorts have effectively surrendered and the momentum of this rebound would likely be over.

TAC has +78% volume, but the volume is only 0.9x the average volume—rising on shrinking volume. I got burned by something like this last week: I saw the low-volume surge and thought it would pull back, but they pushed it up for three more days… Fair enough, I’m that kind of cautious. But seriously, that volume-price divergence always makes me feel uneasy. It’s about 8% from resistance 0.0047 to 0.00512. Support is at 0.003388. The risk-reward isn’t easy to calculate because the middle distance is too wide. I’m not really inclined to touch it for a short-term trade. For a mid-term setup, we’d need to see whether it can break 0.00512 with volume—then we can look.

BTC is down 1.8% to 78081 today, and ETH has also pulled back to 2451, but over 7 days BTC is still +19.7% and ETH is +26.3%. The overall market is still in a repair phase. The Fear & Greed Index is 50—neutral, not cold and not hot. In this kind of sentiment, the best strategy, in my opinion, is—don’t chase a move that’s already run wild. Wait for a pullback and build positions in batches for projects whose fundamentals are still intact. After all, at a value of 50, you’re not in an extremely fearful “golden bottom” nor in a greed-overheated top. It’s one of those awkward ranges where anything can happen.

I missed a similar opportunity before. I saw altcoins explode upward and didn’t board in time, and then they kept rallying for three straight days… (Yes, I’m that timid.) So this time my stance is: for something like BTR that has already quadrupled, I’d rather wait for a pullback or wait for a breakout confirmation rather than chase when it’s already in the 95% zone. For ONG, the combination of negative funding and rising with volume could be worth trying with a small position—but the stop-loss must be set properly.

What do you think—does this BTR move mark the start of the BitVM narrative, or is it the top of short-term sentiment? Drop your thoughts in the comments. I’d like to see if there are friends hesitating like me.
